sentences.text: Prestosuchus is an extinct genus of pseudosuchian, a group within Loricata, that lived in Brazil during the Middle Triassic.
This animal possessed a deep skull and serrated teeth similar to its relatives.
The premaxilla, the front bone of the upper jaw, has a tall, boxy main body containing four teeth.
The maxilla, the main upper jaw bone, is deep and roughly textured, featuring a low triangular antorbital fenestra and 11 to 13 large teeth.
The holotype, the specimen the species is based on, of Prestosuchus chiniquensis was discovered by Wilhelm Rau alongside the holotype of Rauisuchus tiradentes.
These fossils were found in 1928 or 1929 within the Santa Maria Formation at the Paleontological Site Chiniquá near São Pedro do Sul, Brazil.
Friedrich von Huene named the genus Prestosuchus in 1938 to honor the Brazilian paleontologist Vicentino Prestes de Almeida.
The Chiniquá fossil site is now part of the Paleorrota geopark.
Prestosuchus likely walked on four legs with an upright semi-erect stance, having limb bones positioned below the hips, unlike modern crocodilians.
Researchers suggest that the leg musculature of Prestosuchus represents a primitive condition for archosaurs rather than a derived one.
Prestosuchus was likely an apex predator in its habitat.
Prestosuchus has historically been classified as a rauisuchian and as the defining member of the family Prestosuchidae.
The type species of the genus Prestosuchus is P. chiniquensis, described by von Huene in 1942.
The fossil range of Prestosuchus is the Middle Triassic, specifically the Ladinian stage.
All undisputed fossils of Prestosuchus come from the lower Santa Maria Formation in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
It is debated whether the groups Rauisuchia and Prestosuchidae are valid, as Rauisuchia is considered paraphyletic and Prestosuchidae is polyphyletic in its widest form.
There is an ongoing debate regarding the exact number of species contained within the genus Prestosuchus.
Some researchers have suggested that Procerosuchus celer and Prestosuchus loricatus are junior synonyms of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.

Researchers Kischlat and Barberena (1999) proposed that certain Prestosuchus fossils, including the paralectotype of P. chiniquensis and the Porto Alegre specimen, should be classified as a new genus and species.
